notes:
START: null, deliberately. The header says 'Varies. See Below' and names no NPC, and chronicle_snpc for this row is the string 'varies. promathia mission 3-3#walkthrough' -- a scraped pointer, not an entity. Leaving start.npc null means giver_of falls back to that same chronicle value and nothing moves; the alternative, picking one of the two nations' first NPCs, would invent a giver for a mission whose whole point is that it has two entrances. The effective start is a zone line either way: Northern San d'Oria or Windurst Waters.

The page has NO Walkthrough section; all 24 steps come from the eight sibling sections, whose bullets each restart at [1]. Every note names the section it came from.

STRUCTURE: this is an AND of two paths, not an OR. San d'Oria (Vicissitudes -> Descendants of a Line Lost -> Louverance) and Windurst (Comedy of Errors I and II -> Parradamo Tor -> Exit Stage Left) must both be finished before Cid in the Metalworks closes the mission. Each path is strictly ordered inside itself, but the two are unordered relative to each other, and `group` cannot say that -- a group draws all its members at once, which would light up fifteen NPCs. So they are laid out as one spine in the page's own order, San d'Oria first, and this note is the record that the other order is equally valid. A player who does Windurst first is carried forward by the key items anyway.

EVIDENCE: the Windurst path is the one place in this lane with real observables, and none of them are in the Reward field (which is empty). Cracked Mimeo Mirror on Honoi-Gomoi, Mimeo Jewel on the Loose Sand, and the three feathers together on the Cradle of Rebirth -- four distinct key items, no item used twice. The Jewel shatters if you zone before reaching the peak; if that happens the mark correctly falls back to the Loose Sand, which is where you have to go.

LOST CONTENT: Act II bullet [6] says to read four points before clicking the Loose Sand a second time, and those four points are not in the rendered page. Recorded on the step; it is the reason for medium along with the missing walkthrough.

Everything from step 5 on comes from the 'Opening the Doors', 'The Old Professor' and 'Wrapping Up' sections, whose bullets each restart at [1].

THE DOOR IS AN OR AND IT IS MODELLED. The large door with two keyholes at (H-7) opens either with the pair of crest keys -- Coral to the small hole, Sealion to the large one, within a couple of seconds, the Coral one breaking -- or outright with the [KI] Temple Knight key from the quest A Hard Day's Knight. That is exactly items vs items_alt, so both routes are on the record. The page never gives the door a name, only a description, so it carries no target and no marker; that is the honest reading, not a gap I could close by inventing one.

The door is passed TWICE, out and back, which is why the page keeps warning about a second Coral Crest Key. Both crossings are steps because the page really does make you do it twice.

EVIDENCE: exactly one, the [KI] Reliquiarium key from the ??? after Old Professor Mariselle. The Reward field is empty on this page, so hard rule 7 does not touch it, and the key is not consumed within this mission.

Medium because the Sacrarium maze re-arranges with the Vana'diel day and the addon cannot see the day -- the page just points at a map per day.

the maze in the southeast of Map 1; get to connection point B, which puts you on the southwest of Map 2. The layout changes with the Vana'diel day and the addon cannot see the day.

'Opening the Doors' [3]-[5]: the Coral Crest Key is a rare drop off Fomors on Map 2 and may take many; the Sealion Crest Key comes from the NM Keremet, who is at the end of two hallways lined with six Azren Kuba each -- they all aggro when you engage him but die fast. Farm TWO Coral Crest Keys if you mean to come back out through the door. Skippable entirely if someone already holds the Temple Knight key.

'Opening the Doors' [1]-[2] and [6]: the page calls it only 'the large door with 2 keyholes' and never names it, so there is nothing to mark. Coral to the small keyhole, then Sealion to the large one the moment you hear the click; the Coral key breaks on use and the window is short. The [KI] Temple Knight key opens it outright -- it comes from the quest A Hard Day's Knight, whose keys are traded to Quelveuiat on the middle floor of Tavnazian Safehold (I-10), and which may first want Splinterspine Grukjuk dead at the ??? at (H-10) in Lufaise Meadows.
'Opening the Doors' [7]: right at the fork past the door, for a cutscene

'The Old Professor' [1]: he pops at random from the desk ??? in one of six classrooms, three north and three south, and only for players actually on this mission. He arrives with two Pupils. Clear the Fomor first -- popping him drops your Sneak, and Fomor Hate plus no Sneak in a room full of Fomor is instant aggro. He warps around during the fight.
'The Old Professor' [2]: everyone on the mission checks the ??? after the kill. The Reward field is empty on this page, so the Reliquiarium key is a legitimate observation rather than a reward.

'Wrapping Up' [1]: the same unnamed two-keyhole door, from the other side. This is the second crossing the page keeps warning about -- a second Coral Crest Key unless someone holds the Temple Knight key, or you leave a party member behind to work the switch.
'Wrapping Up' [2]: the same Wooden Gate again; this cutscene ends the mission
